FIDO CTAP 2.3 Conformance Test Report — All 20 Categories (325 / 325 100.00% PASS, 410 Total), §12.2 CredBlob Storage Limits & Non-Discoverable Credential Coverage (P-2 Enhancement, P-4, P-5, F-1 — 6 / 6 PASS), noMcGaPermissionsWithClientPin (+6 ClientPin2 Tests & P-1 Option Dependency Validation), §6.8.7 RP Identifier Truncation (P-7) & RP-Scoped cm(0x04) permissionsRPID Enforcement (+9 CredManAPI Tests), §6.4 & §6.6 Post-Reset encIdentifier & encCredStoreState Plaintext Regeneration & pcmr Rotation, AuthenticatorConfig Negative Matrix (F-1..F-6) & §6.11.4 Token Invalidation, 18 Algorithms (Including Draft NIST FIPS 206 FN-DSA-512 & FN-DSA-1024), Stateless ML-DSA-87 (alg: -50) & ES384 (alg: -35) Root CA Hierarchy, All 10 Extensions (incl. "previewSign", "previewSign5" & "mtc-debug"), Enterprise Attestation & Consolidated Post-Quantum fmt: "mtc"

Multi-log hardware verification on the Nordic nRF52840 DK running Fidont across the last 13 conformance runs (Runs 46–58), highlighted by Run 58 (325 / 325 100.00% PASS, 85 Skipped, 0 Failed, 410 Total in 20m 47.77s across 52,989 debug log lines and 105,346 USB bus records in totalphase_fidont_ctap23.csv) featuring +3 new CredBlob (CTAP 2.3 §12.2) storage limits & non-discoverable credential conformance tests (6 / 6 PASS in credBlob.js, expanding Extensions from 68 to 71 passed: P-2 MakeCredential extension output credBlob: true assertion, P-4 exact maxCredBlobLength 32-byte boundary storage & retrieval, P-5 non-discoverable rk: false credential credBlob storage & allowList retrieval, and F-1 over-limit maxCredBlobLength + 1 = 33-byte credBlob extension rejection with credBlob: false on MakeCredential and empty h'' on GetAssertion without whole-request failure), alongside Run 57's +6 noMcGaPermissionsWithClientPin (CTAP 2.3 §§6.4, 6.5.2.1, 6.5.5.7.1–6.5.5.7.3) conformance tests, Run 56's +9 CredManAPI tests (13 -> 22 passed: CTAP 2.3 §6.8.7 RP Identifier Truncation P-7 and RP-scoped cm(0x04) token permissionsRPID enforcement across subcommands 0x01..0x07), 4-part AuthenticatorConfig F-6 & NFC-safe compact F-5 overflow validation, CTAP 2.3 §6.4 and §6.6 post-reset encIdentifier and encCredStoreState decrypted 128-bit plaintext regeneration & persistent pcmr(0x40) token rotation, §6.11.4 Step 7 immediate invalidation of pre-issued ordinary and persistent pcmr (0x40) tokens when authenticatorConfig forces a PIN change, ExtensionPreviewSign v4 (19/19) and v5 (23/23), and cross-batch-key attestation wire-size and Host USB + MCU RTT timing benchmarks across all 18 supported algorithms.

Attribution & Scope of Fidont: Fidont is an authenticator simulator designed for prototyping new specifications and testing authenticator conformance tools. It is based on the Google OpenSK Rust codebase. Fidont is not suitable for production security use outside of certification, conformance testing, and prototyping new features.

    §1.1 Specification vs. Implementation in Fidont
    §1.2 How ClientPin1 vs. ClientPin2 Construct F-2 and F-3

Fidont authenticator simulator platform performance numbers are for relative comparison as implemented with amateur optimization by me:)

Important

Attribution & Scope of Fidont: Fidont is an authenticator simulator designed for prototyping new specifications and testing authenticator conformance tools. It is based on the Google OpenSK Rust codebase. However, Fidont is not suitable for production security use outside of certification, conformance testing, and prototyping new features.

Overview of the Last 13 Test Runs (Runs 46–58: CredBlob Storage Limits & Non-Discoverable Credential Coverage (P-2 Enhancement, P-4, P-5, F-1 under §12.2), noMcGaPermissionsWithClientPin (+6 Tests under §§6.4, 6.5.2.1, 6.5.5.7.1–6.5.5.7.3), RP Identifier Truncation (P-7 under §§6.8.3, 6.8.4, 6.8.7) & RP-Scoped cm(0x04) Token permissionsRPID Enforcement (§§6.5.5.7.1, 6.8.2–6.8.6), Post-Reset encIdentifier & encCredStoreState 128-Bit Plaintext Regeneration & pcmr Rotation (§6.4, §6.6), AuthenticatorConfig Raw-Command Negative Matrix (F-1..F-6) & State Non-Mutation Verification (§6.11, §6.11.4), Immediate Ordinary & Persistent (pcmr) Token Invalidation When authenticatorConfig Forces a PIN Change (§6.11.4 Step 7), Decrypted encCredStoreState 128-Bit Plaintext Mutation & Stability Verification (§§6.4, 6.1.2, 6.8.5, 6.8.6), Persistent Read-Only Credential Management (pcmr, 0x40) Enforcement (§6.5.5.7.2, §6.5.5.7.3, §6.8.5, §6.8.6) & Direct Native arm64 Beagle USB 12 Capture, [P2] WebAuthn Level 4 Credential Public Key Policy Enforcement (validateCredentialPublicKeyCose Across verifyAttestationByFmt, verifyMtc, verifyPacked, P-02 & P-06), [P2] Generic EdDSA (Ed25519 vs. Ed448) Provider Parity & Algorithm Context Separation (JOSE vs. Credential vs. Generic COSE), [P1/P2] Imported alg Descriptor Boundary & Private Brand Enforcement, Algorithm Descriptor (PS256 PSS, ieee-p1363 vs. der, COSE_Key & crit Header Binding), Production cryptodep.js JWS Bridge + Electron Smoke Test, P1 Signed-Envelope Binding, sandbox.js Proxy + GetNextAssertion UP Fix, Multi-Batch-Key Comparison (ES256, ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, ML-DSA-87), Unified js/mtc-validation.js Attestation Verifier & 3×18 Attestation Matrix P-06)

Important

Executive Summary of Run 58 (fido_conformance_debug.log L1–L52989 & totalphase_fidont_ctap23.csv 105,346 USB bus records (9.73 MB), 325 Passed / 85 Skipped / 0 Failed (410 Total) across all 20 CTAP 2.3 Categories in 20m 47.77s):

  1. Closing the credBlob Storage Limits & Non-Discoverable Credential Partial-Coverage Gap (CTAP 2.3 §12.2):
    • Prior Coverage Gap: Previously, credBlob.js only checked getInfo.maxCredBlobLength >= 32 (P-1), an in-range random credBlob without asserting the MakeCredential extension output (P-2), and a credential created without credBlob (P-3). No test exercised exact maxCredBlobLength boundary storage, over-limit (maxCredBlobLength + 1) handling, or non-discoverable (options.rk = false) credentials.
    • Normative CTAP 2.1 / 2.2 / 2.3 §12.2 (#sctn-credBlob-extension) Requirements:
      • Exact Maximum Boundary (P-4): When credBlob.byteLength === maxCredBlobLength, MakeCredential with options.rk = true MUST store the blob, emit authData.extensionsData['credBlob'] === true (a16863726564426c6f62f5), and return the full maxCredBlobLength-byte buffer on GetAssertion({"credBlob": true}).
      • Non-Discoverable Credentials (P-5, options.rk = false): Per §12.2, when getInfo.options.rk is true, the authenticator MUST support credBlob for discoverable credentials and MAY also support credBlob for non-discoverable credentials (returning credBlob: true if stored in the wrapped credential handle, as in OpenSK/Fidont CredentialSource, or credBlob: false if declined); when getInfo.options.rk is not true, the authenticator MUST support credBlob for non-discoverable credentials (credBlob: true). Subsequent GetAssertion({"credBlob": true}) with allowList MUST return credBlobBytes when makeCredExt['credBlob'] === true and h'' (Uint8Array(0)) when makeCredExt['credBlob'] === false.
      • Over-Limit credBlob (F-1, credBlob.byteLength === maxCredBlobLength + 1) Without Assuming Whole-Request Failure: Per §12.2 ("To denote failure in storing credBlob, the authenticator MUST include the following extension data in the authenticatorData structure: { 'credBlob': false }") and §6.1 / §6.2 general extension processing, an over-limit credBlob does not require the entire MakeCredential command to fail. If MakeCredential succeeds (statusCode === 0x00), authData.extensionsData['credBlob'] MUST NOT be true (false or omitted) and a subsequent GetAssertion({"credBlob": true}) MUST return an empty byte string h'' (a16863726564426c6f6240), proving the over-limit blob was neither stored nor silently truncated to maxCredBlobLength.

Executive Summary of Run 55 (fido_conformance_debug.log L1–L49960, totalphase_fidont_ctap23.csv 81,501 USB records & opensk_rtt.log, 313 Passed / 79 Skipped / 0 Failed across all 20 CTAP 2.3 Categories in 19m 27.21s Active Bus Time):

  1. Closing the Post-Reset Encrypted Identifier (encIdentifier, 0x19) & Store-State (encCredStoreState, 0x1E) Plaintext Regeneration Assertion Gap (CTAP 2.3 §6.4 & §6.6):
    • Gap in Existing Conformance Suite: Previously, Authr-Generic-1.js P-4 (encIdentifier) and P-5 (encCredStoreState) decrypted pre-reset snapshots (decryptedEnc1, decryptedEnc2) to verify pre-reset stability, but after sendReset() only compared the 16-byte AES-128-CBC ciphertext block (assert.notDeepEqual(ct2, ct3)). Because single-block AES-128-CBC (C = E_K(P XOR IV)) is a bijection over 128-bit blocks, any fresh 16-byte IV (iv3 !== iv2) or rotated persistentPinUvAuthToken key K changes ct3 even if the authenticator failed to regenerate the underlying 128-bit identifier or credStoreState plaintext P.
    • New Post-Reset Decryption & Plaintext Regeneration Verification Added (Authr-Generic-1.js:551-825):
      1. Captures and decrypts two consecutive pre-reset authenticatorGetInfo(0x04) responses (getInfo1, getInfo2) using the pre-reset persistent pcmr(0x40) token (pinToken.pinUvAuthToken), verifying iv2 !== iv1 and decryptedEnc2.toString('hex') === decryptedEnc1.toString('hex') (16 bytes / 128 bits).
      2. Sends authenticatorReset(0x07) and captures the immediate post-reset getInfo3 snapshot (transformedEncIdentifier3 / transformedEncCredStoreState3).
      3. Calls configurePinUv() and getTestPinUVAuthTokenWithPermissions(ClientPin2Permissions.pcmr) to obtain the post-reset persistent token (postResetPinToken.pinUvAuthToken), asserting postResetPpuatHex !== preResetPpuatHex (resetPersistentPinUvAuthToken() per CTAP 2.3 §6.6).
      4. Decrypts getInfo3 using postResetPinToken.pinUvAuthToken via HKDF-SHA-256(..., info="encIdentifier" | "encCredStoreState") + AES-128-CBC (16 bytes), and asserts postResetPlaintextHex !== preResetPlaintextHex — proving the 128-bit identifier (P-4) and 128-bit credStoreState (P-5) plaintexts were regenerated on reset.
      5. Captures a subsequent post-reset getInfo4 snapshot and verifies that post-reset getInfo calls continue rotating the 16-byte IV (iv4 !== iv3) while preserving the new post-reset 128-bit plaintext (decryptedEnc4.toString('hex') === postResetPlaintextHex).

Run 52 (16:20:47 – 16:39:27 PST / 00:20:47 – 00:39:27 UTC, 2026-11-01, 18m 28.64s) Full 20-Category CTAP 2.3 Conformance (307 / 307 100.00% PASS) With Decrypted 128-Bit encCredStoreState Plaintext Mutation & Stability Verification (§§6.4, 6.1.2, 6.8.5, 6.8.6) & Direct Native arm64 Beagle USB 12 Capture (93,835 USB Records)

Important

Executive Summary of Run 52 (fido_conformance_debug.log L1–L46183, totalphase_fidont_ctap23.csv 93,835 USB records & opensk_rtt.log, 307 Passed / 79 Skipped / 0 Failed across all 20 CTAP 2.3 Categories in 18m 28.64s):

  1. Closing the encCredStoreState Single-Block AES-128-CBC Ciphertext Assertion Gap (CTAP 2.3 §§6.4, 6.1.2, 6.8.5 & 6.8.6):
    • Cryptographic Gap in Existing Suite: Previously, ResidentKey.js P-5 and CredentialManagement-UpdateAndDelete.js P-1 / P-2 only asserted ivNew !== ivOld and ctNew !== ctOld after discoverable credential creation, updateUserInformation(0x07), and deleteCredential(0x06). Because encCredStoreState is a single 16-byte AES-128-CBC block (encCredStoreState = IV || E_K(credStoreState XOR IV)), and E_K is a bijective permutation over 128-bit blocks, any change in the 16-byte IV (IV_1 !== IV_2) mathematically guarantees a different 16-byte ciphertext (E_K(P XOR IV_1) !== E_K(P XOR IV_2)) even when the underlying 128-bit plaintext P = credStoreState never changed.
    • Decryption & Plaintext Mutation Assertions Added:
      • Added parseAndDecryptEncCredStoreState(encCredStoreStateHex, pcmrPinUvAuthToken) using window.navigator.fido.fido2.crypto.decryptAES128CBC(raw, pcmrPinUvAuthToken, "encCredStoreState") (HKDF-SHA-256(IKM=pcmrToken, salt=0x00^32, info="encCredStoreState", L=16) per CTAP 2.3 §6.4).
      • Retained a valid persistent pinUvAuthToken with pcmr (0x40) permission across subsequent transient mc (0x01) and cm (0x04) token acquisitions (which per CTAP 2.3 §6.5.5.7.2 do not invalidate the persistent pcmr token).
      • Verified in ResidentKey.js P-5 (MakeCredential with rk: true), CredentialManagement-UpdateAndDelete.js P-1 (updateUserInformation(0x07)), and P-2 (deleteCredential(0x06)):
        1. Pre-mutation read stability: Two consecutive authenticatorGetInfo calls before mutation produce fresh IVs (snap2.iv !== snap1.iv) and identical 128-bit plaintext (snap2.ptHex === snap1.ptHex).
        2. Post-mutation plaintext change: After the credential store mutation, authenticatorGetInfo decrypted with the same retained pcmr token produces a fresh IV (snap3.iv !== snap2.iv), changed ciphertext (snap3.ct !== snap2.ct), and a new 128-bit plaintext credStoreState (snap3.ptHex !== snap2.ptHex).
        3. Post-mutation read stability: A subsequent authenticatorGetInfo call with no further mutation produces a fresh IV (snap4.iv !== snap3.iv) while preserving the new 128-bit plaintext (snap4.ptHex === snap3.ptHex).
      • Verified in CredentialManagement-UpdateAndDelete.js F-1 and F-2 that rejected pcmr-only updateUserInformation(0x07) and deleteCredential(0x06) attempts (CTAP2_ERR_PIN_AUTH_INVALID(0x33)) generate a fresh IV (snapAfter.iv !== snapBefore.iv) while leaving the decrypted 128-bit plaintext credStoreState unchanged (snapAfter.ptHex === snapBefore.ptHex).
  2. Rebuilt & Provisioned ML-DSA-44 Batch & Enterprise Attestation Keys + Direct Native arm64 Beagle USB 12 Capture (93,835 USB Records):
    • Rebuilt runner-nordic (nrf52840dk with debug enabled), provisioned ML-DSA-44 (alg: -48) batch and enterprise keys via tools/configure.py, and captured 93,835 hardware USB bus records (8,636,658 bytes) in totalphase_fidont_ctap23.csv via capture_usb12.

Executive Summary of Run 51 (fido_conformance_debug.log L1–L45718, totalphase_fidont_ctap23.csv 92,870 USB records & opensk_rtt.log L293865+, 307 Passed / 79 Skipped / 0 Failed across all 20 CTAP 2.3 Categories in 18m 27.22s):

  1. Persistent Read-Only Credential Management (pcmr, 0x40) Conformance Coverage & OpenSK Firmware Patch:
    • CTAP 2.3 Spec Requirements (§6.5.5.7.2, §6.5.5.7.3, §6.8.5 & §6.8.6):
      • Under §6.5.5.7.2 (getPinUvAuthTokenUsingPinWithPermissions) and §6.5.5.7.3 (getPinUvAuthTokenUsingUvWithPermissions), the pcmr (0x40) permission MUST NOT be combined with any other defined permission (cm, mc, ga, etc.) and MUST NOT be granted if perCredMgmtRO is absent or false in authenticatorGetInfo.options; any such request MUST fail with CTAP2_ERR_UNAUTHORIZED_PERMISSION (0x40).
      • Under §6.8.5 (deleteCredential) and §6.8.6 (updateUserInformation), both write subcommands require a pinUvAuthToken with the cm (0x04) permission; a pcmr-only (0x40) token MUST be rejected with CTAP2_ERR_PIN_AUTH_INVALID (0x33) and leave stored credentials unmodified.
    • OpenSK Firmware Fix (libraries/opensk/src/ctap/client_pin.rs):
      • Updated ClientPin::check_permissions to reject any permission mask that combines PERSISTENT_CREDENTIAL_MANAGEMENT_READ_ONLY (0x40) with any other bit (permissions != PERSISTENT_CREDENTIAL_MANAGEMENT_READ_ONLY) with Ctap2StatusCode::CTAP2_ERR_UNAUTHORIZED_PERMISSION (0x40), alongside credential_management.rs requiring CREDENTIAL_MANAGEMENT (0x04) for DeleteCredential and UpdateUserInformation.
    • 10 New CTAP 2.3 Conformance Negative Tests Added:
      • Authr-ClientPin2-GetPinUvAuthTokenUsingPinWithPermissions.js (F-2..F-5): Tests pcmr|cm (0x44), pcmr|mc (0x41), pcmr|ga (0x42), and pcmr (0x40) when perCredMgmtRO is absent/false via getPinUvAuthTokenUsingPinWithPermissions(0x09), plus restores a valid PIN at the end of F-1 so forcePINChange does not bleed into F-2..F-5.
      • Authr-ClientPin2-GetPinUvAuthTokenUsingUvWithPermissions.js (F-1..F-4): Tests pcmr|cm (0x44), pcmr|mc (0x41), pcmr|ga (0x42), and pcmr (0x40) when perCredMgmtRO is absent/false via getPinUvAuthTokenUsingUvWithPermissions(0x0A).
      • CredentialManagement-UpdateAndDelete.js (F-1 & F-2): Acquires a pcmr-only (0x40) token, attempts updateUserInformation(0x07) (F-1) and deleteCredential(0x06) (F-2), asserts CTAP2_ERR_PIN_AUTH_INVALID(0x33), and enumerates credentials via enumerateCredentialsBegin(0x04) to verify user.id, user.name, and user.displayName remain completely unchanged.
  2. Direct Native arm64 Total Phase Beagle USB 12 Capture (92,870 Indexed Hardware USB Records):
    • Captured directly from the Beagle USB 12 analyzer (port 0) using the native Apple Silicon arm64 C library (beagle-api-macos-arm64-v6.00/c/libbeagle.dylib + capture_usb12) into totalphase_fidont_ctap23.csv (8,546,668 bytes, 92,877 lines, 92,870 indexed USB bus events), bypassing the x86_64 Data Center GUI entirely.

  2. Strict P1 verifyP256Signature Verification Across ExtensionPreviewSign (v4, 19 / 19) & ExtensionPreviewSign5 (v5, 23 / 23) (73 MakeCredential + 49 GetAssertion Exchanges):
    • Fixed a P1 silent-pass bug in verifyP256Signature where @noble/curves p256.verify threw on raw 64-byte (r || s) signatures or high-S values and the catch block fell back to crypto.subtle.verify (which returned false on DER vs. raw IEEE P1363 format), causing positive signature checks to be silently skipped and negative cross-key checks (P-5) to trivially pass.
    • With nobleP256.verify(sigBytes, msgHash, pubUncompressed, { lowS: false }) and the catch fallback removed, every ESP256 (-9), ES256 (-7), ESP256-split (-65600 / -300 / -70009), and ESP256-split-ARKG (-65601 / -65539 under ARKG-P256 -65700) signature in ExtensionPreviewSign (v4) and ExtensionPreviewSign5 (v5) is cryptographically verified end-to-end.
  3. 18-Algorithm Post-Quantum & Composite Attestation Telemetry (ML-DSA-44 Batch & Enterprise Keys, Host IPC vs. MCU RTT):
    • All 11 PQ + Composite — "packed" (10,945.3 B / 186.0f, 8,806 B ML-DSA-44 X.509 attStmt): Host 1,637.6 ms (median 1,449.5 ms), MCU RTT 864.4 ms (median 636.4 ms) $\implies$ 773.2 ms (4.16 ms/frame) Host–MCU USB overhead.

Run 41 (22:24:31 – 22:38:25 UTC, 2026-10-30, 13m 54.02s) Full-Suite Conformance (260 / 260 100.00% PASS): Electron 45 Dependency Update, HID Path Re-Resolution & Re-Provisioned ML-DSA-65 Batch (--mtc-x5c) / ML-DSA-44 Enterprise Keys + Simultaneous Host USB & MCU RTT Timing

Important

Executive Summary of Run 41 (fido_conformance_debug.log L1–L37842 & opensk_rtt.log L124833–L133952, 260 Passed / 30 Skipped / 0 Failed / 0 Lockups in 13m 54.02s):

  1. 100% PASS (260 / 260) over USB HID on Electron 45.1.0 with the updated dependency tree (node-abi 4.40.0, node-hid 2.2.0, usb 2.19.1, @stoprocent/noble 2.8.0, express 4.22.3, body-parser 1.20.9, nan 2.30.0, node-gyp 12.4.0; native modules rebuilt for Electron 45.1.0). 0 [ASSERTION FAILED], 0 status: false waits, and 0 MCU [WARN]/[ERROR]/panic lines across 159 Host / 160 MCU MakeCredential exchanges.
  2. HID path re-resolution (hiddep.js getDeviceState): on macOS the DevSrvsID:<id> path changes whenever the authenticator re-enumerates. A first attempt on the new stack (without the fix) failed P-4 after 187 passes because every automatic probe-rs MCU reset left the app waiting 30 s on a stale path. The fix rebinds to the single device with matching VID/PID/serial and refreshes the path in place; it fired 5 times in this run and every test continued.
  3. Re-provisioned attestation keys (tools/configure.py --mtc --mtc-x5c --enterprise): ML-DSA-65 batch key (MTC descriptor 7,889 B including the batch x5c) plus the classical ES256 second batch key (cX5c 600 B), and the ML-DSA-44 enterprise key (serial 123456, 6,644 B). An intermediate run without --mtc-x5c turned PQ "packed" into self-attestation (not comparable) and is superseded by this run.
  4. Simultaneous Host USB & MCU RTT benchmark, ML-DSA-65 batch key (alg: -49):
    • All 11 PQ + Composite — "packed" (12,469.3 B / 211.8f, 10,335 B attStmt): Host USB mean 2,875.2 ms (median 2,736.0 ms), MCU mean 2,001.1 ms (median 1,838.8 ms) $\implies$ 874.2 ms (4.13 ms/frame) pure USB overhead.
    • All 11 PQ + Composite — "mtc" (5,490.3 B / 93.5f, 3,351 B attStmt): Host USB mean 2,105.1 ms (median 2,194.7 ms), MCU mean 1,704.6 ms (median 1,783.3 ms) $\implies$ 400.5 ms (4.28 ms/frame), saving 770.2 ms (-26.8%) mean / 541.3 ms median Host USB time, 473.6 ms pure USB transfer and 6,979 B (118.3 frames) per PQ registration.

Run 37 (02:33:31 – 03:23:28 PDT, 2026-10-30, 14m 03.04s Active Execution) Full-Suite Conformance (260 / 260 100.00% PASS): [P2] Generic EdDSA (Ed25519 vs. Ed448) Provider Parity & Algorithm Context Separation + Simultaneous Host USB & MCU RTT Attestation Timing Analysis (ML-DSA-65 Batch Key)

Important

Executive Summary of Run 37 (fido_conformance_debug.log L1–L38147 & opensk_rtt.log L63843–L73102, 260 Passed / 30 Skipped / 0 Failed / 0 Lockups in 14m 03.04s active execution / 49m 56.29s wall-clock):

  1. [P2] Generic EdDSA (Ed25519 vs. Ed448) Provider Parity & Algorithm Context Separation (js/mtc-validation.js & dependencies/cryptodep.js):
    • Generic EdDSA ('EdDSA' / COSE -8) Subtype Resolution (mtc-validation.js:1654-1823, dependencies/cryptodep.js:938-1150): Generic 'EdDSA' / -8 resolves its required public key byte length (32 B vs. 57 B) and raw signature byte length (64 B vs. 114 B) from the actual supported key subtype (Ed25519 / crv: 6 vs. Ed448 / crv: 7), while explicit 'Ed448' / COSE -53 remains strictly restricted to Ed448 (crv: 7, 57 B key, 114 B sig). Added extractEd448PubKeyFromPem (OID 1.3.101.113 = 06032b6571) and routed Ed448 X.509 verification through verifyRawEd448 (@noble/curves/ed448) so standalone OpenSSL and packaged Electron 41.7.0 BoringSSL verify Ed448 certificates identically.
    • Algorithm Context Separation (RFC 7518 §3.4 JOSE vs. WebAuthn §5.8.5 Credential Keys vs. RFC 9053 §2.1 Generic COSE Attestation / Checkpoint, mtc-validation.js:1888-2218 & dependencies/cryptodep.js:761-828):
      • JOSE (context: 'jws' & string 'structured-envelope', RFC 7518 §3.4): ES256, ES384, ES512, and ES256K strictly bind their single curve (P-256, P-384, P-521, secp256k1) and fixed-width ieee-p1363 encoding (64, 96, 132, 64 bytes).
      • WebAuthn Credential Public Keys (context: 'credential-cose', WebAuthn §5.8.5): Enforces -7/-9 $\to$ crv: 1 (P-256), -35/-51 $\to$ crv: 2 (P-384), -36/-52 $\to$ crv: 3 (P-521), and -8/-19 $\to$ crv: 6 (Ed25519) on credential public keys. (Note: During Run 37 itself, 'credential-cose' was only wired into verifyPacked self-attestation and helper unit tests; subsequent post-Run-37 integration wired validateCredentialPublicKeyCose pre-dispatch across verifyAttestationByFmt for "none", "mtc", and "packed", direct verifyMtc, direct verifyPacked (x5c + self), and Authr-MakeCred-Resp-1.js (P-02 & P-06).)
      • Generic COSE Attestation / Checkpoint (context: 'cose' / 'checkpoint' / 'x509' / integer 'structured-envelope', RFC 9053 §2.1): Binds kty: 2 (EC2) and the SHA digest (-7 $\to$ SHA-256, -35 $\to$ SHA-384, -36 $\to$ SHA-512) while validating the key's actual supported curve (crv: 1, 2, 3 plus crv: 8 for -7), coordinate byte lengths (32, 48, 66), on-curve point geometry, and signature length (ieee-p1363 2 * coordLen or strict ASN.1 DER).
  2. Simultaneous Host USB Round-Trip (fido_conformance_debug.log) & Hardware MCU Execution (opensk_rtt.log) Attestation Benchmark with ML-DSA-65 (alg: -49, NIST Level 3) Batch Key (159 Host / 160 MCU MakeCredential Exchanges):
    • All 11 PQ + Composite Algorithms — "packed" (12,469.3 B / 211.8f avg, 10,335 B attStmt with 7,004 B ML-DSA-65 X.509 cert): Mean Host USB = 2,634.3 ms (median 2,378.8 ms, sum 28.98 s), Mean MCU = 1,761.0 ms (median 1,465.9 ms, sum 19.37 s) $\implies$ 873.3 ms (4.12 ms/frame) of pure USB HID wire transfer overhead per registration!
    • All 11 PQ + Composite Algorithms — "mtc" (5,490.3 B / 93.5f avg, 3,351 B attStmt with 19 B mtcKeyRef): Mean Host USB = 1,454.5 ms (P-06) / 1,843.5 ms (before()), Mean MCU = 1,056.8 ms (P-06) / 1,445.4 ms (before()) $\implies$ 397.7–398.1 ms (4.25–4.26 ms/frame) of USB HID wire transfer overhead, saving 1,179.8 ms (-44.8%) in P-06 and 790.8 ms (-30.0%) in before() total Host USB round-trip time, 475.2–475.6 ms (-54.5%) of pure USB wire transfer time, and 6,979 B (118.3 frames) on every post-quantum registration!

Important

Executive Summary of Run 36 (fido_conformance_debug.log L1–L37797 & opensk_rtt.log L54689–L63840, 260 Passed / 30 Skipped / 0 Failed / 0 Lockups in 13m 45.68s):

  1. [P1/P2] Imported alg Descriptor Boundary & Private Brand Enforcement (js/mtc-validation.js & dependencies/cryptodep.js):
    • Closed the descriptor-injection boundary where resolveSignatureAlgorithmSpec previously returned any imported object with string keyType and id:
      • Private Descriptor Brand (mtc-validation.js:349-370): Added closure-private ALG_SPEC_BRAND = Symbol('MtcValidatedAlgorithmSpec') and VALIDATED_ALG_SPECS = new WeakSet(). Only descriptors constructed internally by resolveSignatureAlgorithmSpec carry this brand; verifyEnvelopeSignatureAgainstTrustedRoots, bridgeProvider.verifyCertSignature, and fallbackProvider.verifyCertSignature reject any unbranded object immediately.
      • Strict JWS & Structured Raw alg Schema (mtc-validation.js:1733-1806, mtc-validation.js:2235-2388): Enforced exact, unpadded RFC 7515 §4.1.1 StringOrURI strings at JWS boundaries (jws-compact, jws-descriptor, structured-protected), rejecting imported descriptor objects (ES256 with sigEncoding: 'der', PS256 selecting EC + DER), numeric JWS alg: -7, and whitespace-padded ' ES256 '. In structured-raw, permitted only exact registered strings or COSE safe integers (rejecting unregistered descriptor objects and numeric strings like '-7').
      • Canonical Policy Verification in Production Bridge (dependencies/cryptodep.js:899-959): Hardened verifySignature to look up BUILTIN_ALG_SPECS[HashAlgOrSpec.id] and verify keyType, nodeDigest, rsaPadding, pssSaltLength, p1363SigLength, and context-bound sigEncoding before accepting any descriptor object.
  2. Simultaneous Host USB Round-Trip (fido_conformance_debug.log) & Hardware MCU Execution (opensk_rtt.log) Attestation Benchmark with ML-DSA-65 (alg: -49, NIST Level 3) Batch Key (159 Host / 160 MCU MakeCredential Exchanges):

Important

Executive Summary of Run 35 (fido_conformance_debug.log L1–L39170 & opensk_rtt.log L45564–L54688, 260 Passed / 30 Skipped / 0 Failed / 0 Lockups in 14m 06.34s):

  1. [P1/P2] Validated Algorithm Descriptor Contract (SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM_SPECS), Wire-Encoding Separation (ieee-p1363 vs. der), COSE_Key Family/Curve Binding & RFC 7515 §4.1.11 crit Header Enforcement:
    • Replaced digest-only resolveEnvelopeHashAlg with resolveSignatureAlgorithmSpec(alg, context) and SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM_SPECS, passing a validated algSpec ({ jwsAlg, coseAlg, family, kty, crv, namedCurve, hashAlg, rsaPadding, saltLength, minModulusBits, jwsSignatureEncoding, x509SignatureEncoding, wireEncoding }) into verifySignature and verifySignatureCOSE:
      • RSA Padding & Salt Length (PS256 vs. RS256, RFC 7518 §3.5): Standards-valid PS256 (2048-bit RSA, RSA_PKCS1_PSS_PADDING, saltLength: 32) is now ACCEPTED across jws-compact, jws-descriptor, structured-protected, and structured-raw, while PS256-labelled RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signatures and wrong-salt PSS (saltLength: 16) are REJECTED.
      • Cross-Family & Cross-Curve Key Confusion: RS256-labelled EC signatures (jws-compact, structured-protected, and subtreeCheckpoint), ES256-labelled RSA signatures, and ES256-labelled OKP/Ed25519 COSE_Key batch/device keys are REJECTED (assertCoseKeyMatchesAlgorithmSpec).
      • Wire Encoding (ieee-p1363 vs. der, RFC 7518 §3.4): JWS ECDSA (context: 'jws') strictly requires fixed-width R || S (64 B for ES256/ES256K, 96 B for ES384, 132 B for ES512) and rejects ASN.1 DER Ecdsa-Sig-Value, while CTAP2/X.509 (context: 'x509' / 'cose') preserves DER verification.
      • Critical Header Enforcement (RFC 7515 §4.1.11): validateJwsCriticalHeaders rejects unknown crit extensions (crit: ["exp"]), empty/non-array crit, duplicate entries, standard headers in crit, and missing header parameters.
  2. Simultaneous Host USB Round-Trip (fido_conformance_debug.log) & Hardware MCU Execution (opensk_rtt.log) Attestation Benchmark (159 Host / 160 MCU MakeCredential Exchanges):
    • All 11 PQ + Composite Algorithms — "packed" (14,427.3 B / 245.2f avg): Mean Host USB = 2,833.6 ms (median 2,543.9 ms, sum 31.17 s), Mean MCU = 1,826.3 ms (median 1,498.3 ms, sum 20.09 s) $\implies$ 1,007.3 ms (4.11 ms/frame) of pure USB HID wire transfer overhead per registration!
    • All 11 PQ + Composite Algorithms — "mtc" (6,808.3 B / 115.9f avg): Mean Host USB = 2,136.0 ms (P-06) / 1,954.8 ms (before()), Mean MCU = 1,647.0 ms (P-06) / 1,467.7 ms (before()) $\implies$ 487.1–489.0 ms (4.20–4.22 ms/frame) of USB HID wire transfer overhead, saving 697.6 ms (-24.6%) in P-06 and 878.8 ms (-31.0%) in before() total Host USB round-trip time, 518.3–520.2 ms (-51.5%) of pure USB wire transfer time, and 7,619 B (129.3 frames) on every post-quantum registration!

Important

Executive Summary of Run 33 (fido_conformance_debug.log L1–L39162 & opensk_rtt.log L27316–L36440, 260 Passed / 30 Skipped / 0 Failed / 0 Lockups in 14m 09.70s):

  1. Resolution of All 4 Run 32 ResidentKey.js Errors (P-2, P-3, P-5, P-6 $\to$ 100% Attempt-1 PASS):
    • In Run 32 (17:35:04–17:50:04 PDT), ResidentKey.js P-2 and P-3 failed on authenticatorGetNextAssertion(0x08) with [GetNextAssertion] Response authData.flags.up (false) MUST match requested UP (undefined)!, and their 4 Mocha retries leaked 20 discoverable credentials (4 × 3 + 4 × 2 = 20), causing P-5 and P-6 to fail with CTAP2_ERR_KEY_STORE_FULL(40).
    • Root-cause analysis identified that app/js/sandbox.js:20 used return target[key] || target.window[key] inside its with (sandboxProxy) get trap, causing boolean false stored in lastGetAssertionExpectedUp on the sandbox target scope to short-circuit to target.window.lastGetAssertionExpectedUp (undefined).
    • Fixing app/js/sandbox.js:20 to (key in target) ? target[key] : target.window[key] and synchronizing window.lastGetAssertionExpectedUp in CTAP2.js:1188-1244 resolved all 4 errors: P-1, P-2, P-3, P-5, and P-6 passed on their first attempt with zero retries!
  2. P1 Signed-Envelope Cryptographic Binding & Independent Signer Root Pinning (js/mtc-validation.js):
    • Verified in both standalone unit tests (ALL_MTC_VALIDATION_UNIT_TESTS_PASSED across positive & negative vectors in js/mtc-envelope-vectors.js and js/test-mtc-envelope-binding.js) and the full 38-suite conformance run (260 / 260 PASS):
      • Removed caller-controlled signingInputBytes from imported structured envelopes (raw-cose-sign1-envelope, cose-sign1, jws, raw), reconstructing signing input internally over exact parsed payload bytes.
      • Enforced independent trustedSignerRoots configuration (options.trustedSignerRoots / metadata.attestationRootCertificates), ignoring signedEnvelope.rootCertificates and treating x5c strictly as a candidate chain.
      • Enforced atomic all-or-nothing import before branding any row with Symbol('MtcAuthenticatedBootstrap').
  3. Simultaneous Host USB Round-Trip (fido_conformance_debug.log) & Hardware MCU Execution (opensk_rtt.log) Attestation Timing Dissection:
    • Because Run 33 captured both fido_conformance_debug.log (Host USB ms) and opensk_rtt.log (MCU ms) simultaneously across all 159 valid MakeCredential exchanges (54 in P-06, 18 in before(), 10 in mtcDebug.js + EntepriseAttestation.js), we can directly separate MCU cryptographic execution time from physical USB Full-Speed HID transport overhead (Host USB ms - MCU ms):
      • All 11 PQ + Composite Algorithms — "packed" (14,427.3 B / 245.2f avg): Mean Host USB = 2,908.7 ms, Mean MCU = 1,902.7 ms $\implies$ 1,006.0 ms (4.10 ms/frame) of pure USB HID wire transfer overhead per registration!
      • All 11 PQ + Composite Algorithms — "mtc" (6,808.3 B / 115.9f avg): Mean Host USB = 2,705.0 ms (P-06) / 2,517.2 ms (before()), Mean MCU = 2,217.3 ms (P-06) / 2,030.2 ms (before()) $\implies$ 487.0–487.7 ms (4.20 ms/frame) of USB HID wire transfer overhead, saving 518.3–519.0 ms (-51.6%) of pure USB wire transfer time and 7,619 B (129.3 frames) on every post-quantum registration!

Run 31 (16:27:43 – 16:43:52 PDT, 2026-10-29, 16m 09.10s) Full-Suite Conformance (260 / 260 100.00% PASS): ML-DSA-87 (alg: -50) Batch Attestation Benchmark & Comprehensive Comparison Across All Batch Key Sizes (ES256 P-256 vs. ML-DSA-44 vs. ML-DSA-65 vs. ML-DSA-87)

Important

Executive Summary of Run 31 (opensk_rtt.log L6862–L15997, 260 Passed / 31 Skipped / 0 Failed / 0 Lockups in 16m 09.10s):

  1. Complete 4-Tier Batch Attestation Key Comparison (ES256 P-256 vs. ML-DSA-44 Run 29 vs. ML-DSA-65 Run 30 vs. ML-DSA-87 Run 31):
    • With Run 31 configured to use ML-DSA-87 (alg: -50, NIST Security Level 5, serial: 4098 / 0x0007000000000002) as the authenticator's post-quantum batch attestation key (2,602 B COSE public key, 4,627 B signature, 7,644 B DER X.509v3 leaf certificate signed by the ML-DSA-87 Root CA), we now have full 38-suite conformance benchmarks (159 MakeCredential ceremonies per run) across all three NIST FIPS 204 ML-DSA security levels (ML-DSA-44 in Run 29, ML-DSA-65 in Run 30, ML-DSA-87 in Run 31) alongside the classical ES256 (alg: -7, P-256) batch key:
      • fmt: "packed" Post-Quantum X.509 attStmt Scales from 8,806 B (ML-DSA-44) $\to$ 10,335 B (ML-DSA-65) $\to$ 12,293 B (ML-DSA-87): Because "packed" must carry both the batch key's signature (2,420 B / 3,309 B / 4,627 B) and its X.509v3 leaf certificate (6,364 B / 7,004 B / 7,644 B, which embeds the batch public key plus the 4,627 B ML-DSA-87 Root CA signature), a single MakeCredential "packed" response reaches 13,511–15,068 B (230–256 USB HID frames) with an ML-DSA-87 batch key — consuming up to 92.0% of OpenSK's 16,384 B maxMsgSize buffer!
      • fmt: "mtc" Eliminates 6,339 B (ML-DSA-44), 6,979 B (ML-DSA-65), and 7,619 B (ML-DSA-87) on Every Registration: Because fmt: "mtc" replaces the entire X.509 certificate (6,364 B / 7,004 B / 7,644 B) with a constant 19 B 2-field mtcKeyRef ({ caId, serial }, 24 B CBOR mtcCert), the wire savings of "mtc" over "packed" grow as the batch key size increases:
        • ML-DSA-44 Batch Key (Run 29): attStmt drops from 8,806 B to 2,462 B (-6,344 B / -72.0%); total PQ BCNT drops from 10,024–11,581 B (170–197f) to 3,685–5,242 B (63–89f, saving 6,339 B / 107.4 frames).
        • ML-DSA-65 Batch Key (Run 30): attStmt drops from 10,335 B to 3,351 B (-6,984 B / -67.6%); total PQ BCNT drops from 11,553–13,110 B (196–223f) to 4,574–6,131 B (78–104f, saving 6,979 B / 118.3 frames).
        • ML-DSA-87 Batch Key (Run 31): attStmt drops from 12,293 B to 4,669 B (-7,624 B / -62.0%); total PQ BCNT drops from 13,511–15,068 B (230–256f) to 5,892–7,449 B (100–127f, saving 7,619 B / 129.3 frames).
  2. Zero Lockups Across ThirdPartyPayment & LargeBlobs (opensk_rtt.log L15254–L15997):
    • Verified both root-cause fixes from the lockup analysis (fido_ctap23_lockup_analysis_report.md):
      • ThirdPartyPayment P-2 (L15460–L15503): Sent options: { up: false } in GetAssertion, allowing OpenSK to verify thirdPartyPayment immediately in 1,004.7 ms (398 B response) without blocking on an unprompted physical button press.
      • Authr-LargeBlobs-1 (L15955–L15997): Enforced const maxFragmentLength = (getInfo.maxMsgSize || 1024) - 64; (984 B on 1,048 B write instead of 16,320 B), completing P-1..P-4 and F-1..F-4 in 2.5s with 0 ERR_EXCEEDED_MAX_LENGTH (0x39) errors.
  3. Default Optional UP UX Checkbox (default_optional_up = false) & Universal UP Response Bit Validation:
    • Added a new UI configuration checkbox in app/js/view.js:177-189 ("Default Optional UP in GetAssertion (up=true when omitted)", defaulting to unchecked / false) wired through preload.js:196-203 and CTAP2.js:563-618 (resolveOptionalGetAssertionOptions).
    • Added universal validateResponseAuthDataUpFlag(commandBuffer, responseBuffer) in CTAP2.js:1197-1244 (plus explicit assertions in Authr-GetAssertion-Req-2.js, Authr-GetAssertion-Resp-1.js, and ResidentKey.js) so every successful MakeCredential and GetAssertion response is checked to ensure authData.flags.up matches the effective requested UP (true for MakeCredential and GetAssertion when up !== false; false when up === false).

Executive Summary of Run 30 (fido_conformance_debug.log L1–L37907, 260 Passed / 31 Skipped / 0 Failed in 13m 41.92s):

  1. One Strict, Reusable MTC & Common Attestation Verification Pipeline (js/mtc-validation.js):
    • Consolidated all attestation verification across Authr-MakeCred-Resp-1.js, CTAP2/Protocol/Extensions/mtcDebug.js, and CTAP2/Protocol/Options/EntepriseAttestation.js into a single module (modules/ctap2.3-conformance-module/js/mtc-validation.js, loaded once via manifesto.json):
      • Step 1 (decodeCborLossless & parseAuthDataLossless): Decodes raw CBOR bytes (response.cborBuffer preserved by CTAP2.js:1046-1052) without IEEE-754 Number precision loss, preserving 64-bit uint64 integers (serial, notBefore, notAfter, firmwareVersion) as exact JavaScript BigInt values.
      • Step 2 (Exact Statement & Reference Schema): Requires fmt === "mtc", attStmt keys strictly { alg, sig, mtcCert }, and mtcCert strictly { caId, serial } (19 B mtcKeyRef: caId: 11 B, serial: 8 B uint64). Rejects any extra wire fields on mtcCert (notBefore, notAfter, mtcProof, firmwareVersion, pubKey) so wire references can never self-assert metadata.
      • Step 3 (bootstrapMtcTrustState & Unforgeable Symbol('MtcAuthenticatedBootstrap')): Requires trustedEntries (and optional revocationState, authorizedInventory) to carry an unforgeable private Symbol('MtcAuthenticatedBootstrap') produced only by bootstrapMtcTrustState(), which cryptographically verifies the FIDO-MTC-SUBTREE-CHECKPOINT-V1 signature over every subtree checkpoint against metadata.attestationRootCertificates before branding the table. Resolves the authenticated entry strictly by (caId, serial).
      • Step 4 (Strict mtc-debug Consistency & No Silent Proof Fallback): Validates optional authData.extensions["mtc-debug"] against the resolved authenticated entry (pubKey, notBefore, notAfter, firmwareVersion, rootHash). Treats any malformed supplied mtcProof as an immediate verification error rather than falling back to the proof-free branch.
      • Step 5 (COSE Algorithm Binding & Cryptographic Signature Verification): Binds attStmt.alg to the resolved attestation COSE_Key.alg (kty, crv, key-size invariants) and verifies attStmt.sig over authData || clientDataHash (ML-DSA-44/65/87, FN-DSA-512/1024, SLH-DSA, PQ/T composites, ECDSA, EdDSA, RSA).
      • Step 6 (Validity Window & Revocation Enforcement): Enforces notBefore <= nowSeconds <= notAfter (using BigInt seconds) and checks revocationState (revokedSerials, revokedCaIds, minAllowedFirmwareVersion).
      • Step 7 (RFC 9162 Inclusion Proof & Checkpoint Association): When an inclusion proof is supplied (via mtc-debug or manifest metadata), hashes the canonical leaf (0x00 || leafBytes), walks inclusionPath (0x01 || left || right) within [startIndex, endIndex), and verifies the derived root equals the authenticated checkpoint rootHash.
      • Step 8 (Enterprise Grant & Authorized Inventory Policy): Enforces enterpriseGranted (epAtt === true allowed only when requested for an allowlisted RP; deviceSerial in mtc-debug allowed and required only when epAtt === true) and authorizedInventory serial/deviceSerial policy.
      • Format Dispatch (verifyAttestationByFmt & verifyPacked): Dispatches "none", "packed" (complete X.509v3 leaf checks: version v3, empty Subject DN only when epAtt is true or FIDO id-fido-gen-ce-aaguid matches, BasicConstraints CA:FALSE, validity window, trust chain to metadata.attestationRootCertificates, SPKI / attStmt.alg binding, and signature verification), and "mtc", while rejecting unimplemented formats with unsupported_or_unvalidated.
  2. Key Findings from Run 30 Cross-Format Attestation Wire Size & Timing Analysis (ML-DSA-65 Batch Key vs. ML-DSA-44 Enterprise Key Across 159 MakeCredential Ceremonies):
    • Post-Quantum "packed" with ML-DSA-65 (alg: -49) Batch Certificate Reaches 11,553–13,110 B (196–223 USB HID Frames): In Run 30, the authenticator's batch attestation key is ML-DSA-65 (alg: -49) (sig: 3,309 B, x5c[0]: 7,004 B DER X.509v3 certificate signed by the ML-DSA-87 Root CA $\to$ attStmt = 10,335 B). Across the 11 post-quantum and composite algorithms, fmt: "packed" transmits 11,553–13,110 B (196–223 USB HID frames) per registration and takes a mean of 2,701.7 ms (median: 2,332.3 ms, range: 1,548.1–4,532.5 ms).
    • Post-Quantum fmt: "mtc" with ML-DSA-65 (alg: -49) Batch Key Eliminates 6,979 B (118–119 USB HID Frames) and Saves 1,151.8 ms (-42.6%) per Registration: By replacing the 7,004 B ML-DSA-65 X.509 certificate with the 19 B 2-field mtcKeyRef ({ caId, serial }, 24 B CBOR mtcCert), fmt: "mtc" reduces attStmt from 10,335 B to 3,351 B (-67.6%, -6,984 B), cutting total MakeCredential wire size (BCNT) across all 11 PQ/composite algorithms by 6,979 B (-53.2% to -60.4%, 4,574–6,131 B / 78–104 frames vs. 11,553–13,110 B / 196–223 frames) and reducing mean registration latency from 2,701.7 ms to 1,549.9 ms (-1,151.8 ms / -42.6% faster)!
    • Comparison of Batch (ML-DSA-65, alg: -49) vs. Enterprise (ML-DSA-44, alg: -48) "mtc" + "mtc-debug":
      • Batch "mtc" + "mtc-debug" (mtcDebug.js P-2 & F-3, serial: 4097, ML-DSA-65): authData = 2,578 B (373 B base + 2,205 B 6-field mtc-debug carrying the 1,962 B ML-DSA-65 COSE_Key), attStmt = 3,351 B (3,309 B ML-DSA-65 signature + 24 B mtcCert), total BCNT = 5,949 B (101 frames, 1,812.1–2,735.4 ms) — still 5,604–7,161 B (95–122 frames) smaller than PQ "packed" (11,553–13,110 B)!
      • Enterprise "mtc" + "mtc-debug" (mtcDebug.js P-3 & EntepriseAttestation.js P-2/P-3, serial: 8192, ML-DSA-44): authData = 1,964 B (373 B base + 1,591 B 7-field mtc-debug carrying the 1,322 B ML-DSA-44 COSE_Key + deviceSerial: "123456"), attStmt = 2,462 B (2,420 B ML-DSA-44 signature + 24 B mtcCert), total BCNT = 4,448 B (76 frames, 1,675.2–2,274.8 ms)!

    • Even "mtc" + "mtc-debug" (4,420–4,448 B) Is -57.5% Smaller Than PQ "packed" (10,439 B): Adding the opt-in "mtc-debug" extension (1,565 B non-enterprise / 1,591 B enterprise in authData.extensions) brings ES256 + "mtc" + "mtc-debug" to 4,420–4,448 B (75–76 frames) — still 5,991–6,019 B (101–102 frames) smaller than a single ML-DSA-44 "packed" X.509 registration (10,439 B / 177 frames).

0.0000000000.5 Key Architectural Takeaways from Cross-Format Attestation Benchmarking

  1. fmt: "none" Isolates Pure Credential Key Generation Cost (187.0 ms – 1,783.0 ms):
    • Because fmt: "none" performs zero attestation signing (attStmt = {}, 1 B), its timing directly measures credential key generation + authData assembly + USB transfer:
      • Fastest algorithms (< 400 ms in "none"): FN-DSA-512 (187.0 ms, 1,217 B), FN-DSA-1024 (242.7 ms, 2,113 B), RS256 (258.6 ms, 582 B, pre-generated key), Ed25519 (282.4 ms, 352 B), ML-DSA-44 (309.7 ms, 1,632 B), ES256K (312.5 ms, 388 B), MLDSA44-Ed25519 (358.8 ms, 1,664 B), and ML-DSA-65 (391.7 ms, 2,272 B).
      • Heaviest credential keygen (> 1,400 ms in "none"): Software big-integer ECDSA scalar multiplication on P-384 (ES384: 1,430.0 ms, MLDSA87-ES384: 1,783.0 ms) and P-521 (ES512: 1,438.2 ms) dominates registration latency much more than lattice key generation (ML-DSA-44/65/87 take only 309.7–594.7 ms).
  2. Post-Quantum fmt: "mtc" Saves 6,339 B (107–108 Frames) and 571.0 ms per Registration vs. Post-Quantum fmt: "packed":
    • When registering any of the 11 post-quantum or composite algorithms, both "mtc" and "packed" sign authData || clientDataHash with the same ML-DSA-44 (alg: -48, 2,420 B signature) attestation key.
    • However, "packed" must transmit the 6,364 B X.509v3 ML-DSA-44 leaf certificate (attStmt = 8,806 B, 170–197 USB HID frames), whereas "mtc" transmits only the 19 B mtcKeyRef (attStmt = 2,462 B, 63–89 USB HID frames).
    • Eliminating those 107–108 USB HID IN frames (6,339 B) reduces mean registration latency across the 11 PQ/composite algorithms from 2,045.7 ms ("packed") to 1,474.7 ms ("mtc" in P-06) and 1,405.3 ms ("mtc" in before()) — a 571.0–640.4 ms (27.9%–31.3%) speedup on every registration!
  3. Why Fidont's Default Hybrid Policy ("packed" for Classical, "mtc" for Post-Quantum) Is Optimal:
    • For the 7 classical algorithms, the classical P-256 (ES256, alg: -7) batch X.509 certificate (600 B x5c + 70–72 B signature = 690–692 B attStmt, 1,044–1,275 B BCNT, 18–22 frames) is 1,776 B (30 frames) smaller than "mtc" (2,462 B attStmt with 2,420 B ML-DSA-44 signature).
    • For the 11 post-quantum & composite algorithms, "mtc" (2,462 B attStmt, 3,685–5,242 B BCNT, 63–89 frames) is 6,339 B (107–108 frames) smaller than PQ "packed" (8,806 B attStmt, 10,024–11,581 B BCNT, 170–197 frames).
    • Combining classical "packed" (7 algs) + post-quantum "mtc" (11 algs) yields a total 18-algorithm sweep payload of 58,422 B (999 frames, 24.77 s) vs. 128,150 B (2,181 frames, 32.00 s) for all-"packed" — cutting total wire traffic across the 18-algorithm sweep by 69,728 B (-54.4%, -1,182 USB HID frames)!

W3C WebAuthn Level 4 PR Verification — Consolidated fmt: "mtc" (1,331 B Smaller Wire Payloads) & Opt-In "mtc-debug" Extension: In Run 22 (2026-10-23, 11:51:49.597 – 12:11:56.384 PDT, 20m 06.79s active test execution), we updated both Fidont / OpenSK (mtc.rs, data_formats.rs, mod.rs, configure.py, and fido-mds3.json) and the FIDO CTAP 2.3 Conformance Testing Tool (Authr-MakeCred-Resp-1.js, EntepriseAttestation.js, Metadata-Stmt-1.js) to implement the W3C WebAuthn Level 4 Pull Request (webauthn_level4_pull_request.html):

  • Consolidated fmt: "mtc" Omitting Inline pubKey (1,331 B Wire Reduction): By consolidating mtc-mds into fmt: "mtc" and omitting the inline 1,322 B ML-DSA-44 COSE_Key (pubKey) from attStmt (resolving it instead from metadata.mtcTrustAnchors[].batchKeys by serial), every 2-step PQ and composite MakeCredential response shrank by exactly 1,331 bytes (21 fewer 64-byte CTAPHID IN frames) compared to Run 21:
    • FN-DSA-1024 (-61): 6,067 B $\to$ 4,736 B (6,778.1 ms $\to$ 5,032.7 ms, 1.75s faster over USB HID)
    • ML-DSA-65 (-49): 6,226 B $\to$ 4,895 B (7,387.2 ms $\to$ 6,541.1 ms, 0.85s faster)
    • MLDSA65-Ed25519 (-58): 6,258 B $\to$ 4,927 B (6,775.7 ms $\to$ 6,072.3 ms, 0.70s faster)
    • MLDSA65-ES256 (-55): 6,291 B $\to$ 4,960 B (7,953.1 ms $\to$ 7,428.8 ms, 0.52s faster)
    • ML-DSA-87 (-50): 6,676 B $\to$ 5,345 B (7,240.6 ms $\to$ 5,879.8 ms, 1.36s faster)
    • MLDSA87-Ed448 (-59): 6,688 B $\to$ 5,357 B (7,281.9 ms $\to$ 6,870.0 ms, 0.41s faster)
    • MLDSA87-ES384 (-56): 6,728 B $\to$ 5,397 B (9,136.6 ms $\to$ 8,514.6 ms, 0.62s faster)
  • 100% Pass on Consolidated fmt: "mtc" (Authr-MakeCred-Resp-1 P-01..P-04, F-01) & Metadata-Stmt-1 (25 / 25): All 18 algorithms verified cleanly under P-04 (0.165s), confirming attStmt.pubKey === undefined, batchKeys lookup by serial, RFC 9162 Merkle inclusion proof reduction, HSS-LMS (alg: -46) subtree checkpoint signature verification against metadata.attestationRootCertificates, and ML-DSA-44 batch signature verification.
  • Root Cause & Immediate Fix of the 4 Test-Harness TypeErrors: The only 4 test failures in Run 22 (P-05 in Authr-MakeCred-Resp-1.js, and P-2, P-3, F-6 in EntepriseAttestation.js) occurred in newly added test-harness code that referenced window.config.test.fidoauthenticator.getInfo.extensions synchronously (TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'extensions')) before inspecting the authenticator response. Replacing that synchronous property lookup with the conformance runner's async getGetInfoCached() helper in both test files and repackaging app.asar resolved all 4 harness errors.

0.0000.5 Root-Cause Analysis & Resolution of the 4 Test-Harness TypeErrors (getGetInfoCached())

  1. Observed Symptom (L11307, L18648, L18828, L19421):
    • All 4 failures (P-05 in Authr-MakeCred-Resp-1.js, and P-2, P-3, F-6 in EntepriseAttestation.js) threw the identical JavaScript TypeError inside the test script before sending or inspecting the mtc-debug extension:
      text
      TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'extensions')
  2. Root Cause:
    • Our initial test-harness patch checked window.config.test.fidoauthenticator.getInfo.extensions.includes('mtc-debug'). In the FIDO Conformance Testing Tool, window.config.test.fidoauthenticator does not expose a synchronous .getInfo property (window.config.test.fidoauthenticator.getInfo is undefined); instead, authenticatorGetInfo is retrieved asynchronously via getGetInfoCached().
  3. Fix Applied & Repackaged (app.asar):
    • In Authr-MakeCred-Resp-1.js (P-05), wrapped the test body in return getGetInfoCached().then((getInfo) => { if (!getInfo.extensions || !getInfo.extensions.includes('mtc-debug')) { this.skip(); return; } ... }).
    • In EntepriseAttestation.js, cached supportsMtcDebug = Boolean(getInfo.extensions && getInfo.extensions.includes('mtc-debug')) inside the suite's before() hook (which already invokes getGetInfoCached()) and replaced the synchronous property lookup in P-2, P-3, F-2, F-3, and F-6 with supportsMtcDebug ? { 'mtc-debug': true } : undefined, then repackaged /Applications/FIDO Alliance - Certification Conformance Testing Tools (Patched).app/Contents/Resources/app.asar.

Section 1

Detailed Analysis of Authr-ClientPin2-PinPolicy F-2 Test Logic

1.1 Specification vs. Implementation in Fidont

Per CTAP 2.1 / 2.2 / 2.3 Section 6.5.5.5 (Setting a new PIN):

  • The platform zero-pads newPin into a fixed 64-byte buffer (newPin must be at most 63 UTF-8 bytes so that at least one trailing 0x00 byte terminates the PIN inside the 64-byte plaintext block).
  • The authenticator decrypts newPinEnc using sharedSecret to obtain paddedPin:
    1. If the decrypted paddedPin buffer length is not 64 bytes, the ciphertext parameter itself is malformed (CTAP1_ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER (0x02)).
    2. If the decrypted paddedPin buffer is 64 bytes (PIN_PADDED_LENGTH), the authenticator strips trailing 0x00 bytes and checks the unpadded PIN length: if no 0x00 byte is present (pin.len() == 64 > 63) or if pin_codepoints < minPINLength, it returns CTAP2_ERR_PIN_POLICY_VIOLATION (0x37).

Fidont implements this in client_pin.rs:67-102:

rust
fn decrypt_pin<E: Env>(
    shared_secret: &SharedSecret<E>,
    new_pin_enc: Vec<u8>,
) -> CtapResult<Secret<[u8]>> {
    let decrypted_pin = shared_secret.decrypt(&new_pin_enc)?;
    if decrypted_pin.len() != PIN_PADDED_LENGTH { // PIN_PADDED_LENGTH = 64
        return Err(Ctap2StatusCode::CTAP1_ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER); // 0x02 (2)
    }
    let len = decrypted_pin
        .iter()
        .position(|&c| c == 0)
        .unwrap_or(decrypted_pin.len());
    let mut result = Secret::new(len);
    result.copy_from_slice(&decrypted_pin[..len]);
    Ok(result)
}

1.2 How ClientPin1 vs. ClientPin2 Construct F-2 and F-3

  1. Authr-ClientPin1-PinPolicy.js (F-2 & F-3) — Authr-ClientPin1-PinPolicy.js:112-166: Both F-2 and F-3 generate a 64-byte non-zero PIN inside a 64-byte encryptionBuffer (generateRandomClientPinBuffer(64)). Because decrypted_pin.len() == 64 with no 0x00 terminator, Fidont always returns CTAP2_ERR_PIN_POLICY_VIOLATION (0x37).
  2. Authr-ClientPin2-PinPolicy.js (F-2 vs F-3) — Authr-ClientPin2-PinPolicy.js:109-159:
    • F-3 ("Try setting new pin, that is exactly 64 bytes, and check that Authenticator returns error CTAP2_ERR_PIN_POLICY_VIOLATION(0x37)") encrypts a 64-byte encryptionBuffer (16B IV + 64B CT = 80 bytes) and asserts CTAP2_ERR_PIN_POLICY_VIOLATION (0x37).
    • F-2 ("Try setting new pin, that is bigger than 63 bytes, and check that Authenticator returns an error") generates a random-length buffer generateRandomClientPinBuffer(generateSecureRandomInt(64, 128)) and passes it to encryptAES256CBC (cryptodep.js:394-405), which calls cipher.update(messageBuffer) without cipher.final(), truncating the plaintext to $\lfloor L / 16 \rfloor \times 16$ bytes:
      • When $L \in [64, 79]$ ($24.6\%$ chance), newPinEnc has 64 ciphertext bytes (80B total with IV) $\rightarrow$ CTAP2_ERR_PIN_POLICY_VIOLATION (0x37).
      • When $L \in [80, 128]$ ($75.4\%$ chance), newPinEnc has 80, 96, 112, or 128 ciphertext bytes (96..144B total with IV) $\rightarrow$ CTAP1_ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER (0x02) because decrypted_pin.len() != 64.
    • Updating Authr-ClientPin2-PinPolicy.js:130 to assert.notStrictEqual(ctap2Response.statusCode, CTAP_ERROR_CODES.CTAP1_ERR_SUCCESS) matches the F-2 specification ("check that Authenticator returns an error") and the CTAP 2.1 module.
